newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand signs power purchase pact with Burma.
newsitem.headline: Thailand signs power purchase pact with Burma.

text.p: Thailand on Friday signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Burma agreeing to buy up to 1,500 megawatts of electricity from Rangoon by 2010.
The MOU was signed by visiting Burmese Energy Minister Khin Maung Thein and Sompong Amornviwat, minister in the prime minister's office.

"Both sides still need to discuss in details in future...how many plants would be built to generate 1,500 MW of electricity," said Piyasvasti Amranand, secretary general of Thailand's National Energy Policy Office.
Piyasvasti told Reuters that the total investment cost of the projects to generate both hydropower and natural gas-fuelled power for the sale was about $2.5 billion.
According to the MOU, the Burmese government would select developers to undertake power projects to supply the power to Thailand.
Both parties also agreed to cooperate in the planning and construction of the interconnection of the transmission systems between the two countries.
The Burmese government said it would allow Thai investors to participate in the implementation of power projects under this sale program.

Piyasvasti said that Burma had abundant energy resources to generate power, in particular hydropower, whose technical potential had been estimated at 100,000 MW. Preliminary studies by the Burmese government had revealed that some 196 projects could provide a total generation capacity of 38,000 MW.
